thread.title: GE Is 'Likely' To Get Booted From Dow Index; What Recent Reshuffles Say

author: APARNA NARAYANAN
title: GE Is 'Likely' To Get Booted From Dow Index; What Recent Reshuffles Say
text:
General Electric ( GE ) may be removed from the Dow Jones industrial average, to which it has belonged for more than 110 years, according to a Wall Street analyst.
X GE is one of the original members of the Dow, a price-weighted measure of 30 U.S. blue-chip companies invented by Charles Dow in 1896. The index covers all industries except transportation and utilities.
"We believe the chances that GE could be removed from the Dow are increasing as GE continues to face substantial challenges including earnings and cash pressure, tough global power generation markets, aggressive downsizing, shrinking its portfolio, management shake-up and SEC investigations," Deutsche Bank analyst John Inch wrote Wednesday.
GE's falling share price makes it an "outlier" and "likely candidate for removal" from an index that aims to reflect the "best" large U.S. companies, Inch said.
He sees headline risk if GE were to be dropped from the Dow, noting that roughly 40% of GE's common stock is held by retail investors.
Shares of GE closed up 1.4% at 16.17 on the stock market today , after ending the previous session below 16 for the first time since Dec. 1, 2011.

GE doesn't have to be replaced by another industrial giant, and recent changes show new components don't always come from the same sectors of dropped components.
In the latest tweak, DowDuPont ( DWDP ) replaced DuPont in Sept. 1, 2017, according to S&P Dow Jones Indices, after it merged with Dow Chemical.
Before that, Apple ( AAPL ) replaced AT&T ( T ) on March 19, 2015. And on Sept. 23, 2013, Goldman Sachs ( GS ) replaced Bank of America ( BAC ), Visa ( V ) replaced Hewlett-Packard, which split up, and Nike ( NKE ) replaced Alcoa, which also split up.
A committee made up of three representatives from S&P Dow Jones Indices and two from the Wall Street Journal meets twice a year to consider if any changes are needed to the Dow index.
Committee members prefer the ratio between the highest share price and lowest share price among components to be no more than 10:1. But the current ratio between Boeing ( BA ) (the highest) and GE (the lowest) exceeds 20:1, Deutsche Bank said.
A spokeswoman for S&P Dow Jones Indices declined to comment. "As a matter of firm policy, we do not provide comment on additions or drops to our indices as we consider this information to be market moving and material," she said.
One way for GE to stay in the Dow could be a reverse stock split .
